idea: A signature needs the authentication path of its leaf. Keep, per layer of 5 tree levels, the subtree in use and the next one (built one leaf per signature) instead of recomputing the tree or storing all of it.
change: suites/lms/pqc_suite/lms.c, written from RFC 8554 and RFC 9858 (Cisco hash-sigs was considered and not ported)
checked: RFC vectors byte for byte + selftest + fingerprint
note: Design choice, no measured before: without a cache one signature costs one key generation (43972204 us for this set). Reference hash. 10.7 KB per key, no heap. Height 15 (three layers) is tested on the host only, suites/lms/extra/h15test.c.

idea: A Winternitz step hashes 55 bytes, exactly one SHA-256 block. Build the padded block once per chain and call the compression function, instead of the one-shot hash API for each of 278,000 hashes.
change: suites/lms/pqc_suite/lms.c (hash_short, ots_chain), chosen at run time by lms_fast
note: Reference primitives: 6250 -> 4580 cycles per hash. SHAKE256 H5 W4: 5809905 -> 4814568.

idea: SM3 has the block size and padding of SHA-256, so the same code path serves LMS with SM3 (GmSSL's numbering).
note: before is GmSSL's own lms.c on the same parameter set (suite gmssl_lms, ref), after is this code with the SM3 of components/prims. This code with reference primitives: 11971856.

idea: The opt variant showed no gain from the assembly Keccak: the optimized primitives were not in the image (weak defaults won).
change: linker flags in the suite's CMakeLists.txt; later replaced by WHOLE_ARCHIVE in components/prims
note: The gain is the assembly Keccak of components/prims.

idea: With the SHA accelerator a compression takes about 90 cycles, so the cost is the register traffic. The accelerator starts from the initial value by itself and holds its output as the bytes the next block needs: read 8 words, write 9 back shifted by three bytes, start. No conversion, nothing through memory.
checked: RFC vectors on the device + fingerprint + register model on the host (suites/lms/extra/hwmock)
note: before is the same build with the chains going through the general hardware backend pqc_sha256_compress_opt (-D LMS_HW_CHAIN=off): 641 -> 364 cycles per hash. Against the C SHA-256 (lms-02, 7958379) it is 12.6 times. n = 24: 815747 -> 397402.

idea: components/prims is now linked with WHOLE_ARCHIVE; rebuild without the suite's own linker flags and measure again.
checked: all 15 opt checks + tools/pqc check lms (49 fingerprints equal)
note: No change, as expected: the suite had already pulled the optimized primitives in by name.

idea: The chain step was a loop over n/4 words with the output kept in an array. With straight-line code for n = 32 and n = 24 the eight words stay in registers and the loop overhead goes.
change: suites/lms/pqc_suite/lms_hw.c (the loop stays for other n and behind -D LMS_HW_CHAIN=loop)
checked: RFC 8554 test case 2 and RFC 9858 test case 1 (keygen + sign) on the device + register model on the host
note: 364 -> 272 cycles per hash. n = 24: 397402 -> 299452. H5 W4: 105532 -> 87753. Only these three sets and two vectors were re-run with this code; the other opt rows in results/lms.json are from the loop version.
